function.name: calculate_sunrise_and_sunset
function.description: Calculate the sunrise and sunset time of a location for the given date. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location in city, state format.

date.description: The date for which the sunrise and sunset needs to be calculated in yyyy-mm-dd format.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live clock data, so I can’t tell you the exact current time in New York right now. If you let me know the date (or just check your phone/clock), I can help you figure out what time zone New York would be in and whether daylight‑saving adjustments apply.
message.reasoning:
User asks: "紐約現在是幾點？" (What time is it now in New York?). We need current time. But we don't have real-time data. We can approximate using UTC offset? But we can't guarantee DST. We could respond with "I don't have real-time capability." But maybe we can use an external API? Not allowed. So we should say we cannot provide real-time info. Alternatively, we can compute based on known timezone offset if we assume it's Eastern Time. But we don't know DST status. Could mention that it's currently Eastern Standard or Daylight depending on date. But we don't know date. We can ask user for date/time. But they asked "now". We can answer: "I don't have real-time capability." That might be acceptable.

But maybe we can approximate using the system's current time? We don't have that either. So best to say we cannot provide real-time.
